clue.text: Producer of stamps in Spain?

parts.note: the stamps are not postage but heels struck hard on the floor in a Spanish folk performance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamps' suggests a post office or printing press; the real stamping is done with the feet in a fiery Andalusian art form.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers of this Spanish art form stamp their heels rhythmically, so one of them is literally a maker of stamps.

clue.text: Collar partly tailored from chinchilla pelt

indicators.note: partly says only a portion of the words chinchilla pelt is taken, running across the word break

explanation.surface: A tailor makes a collar out of a chinchilla fur pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the folded part of a jacket front continuing the collar, so it names a type of collar.

clue.text: Meagre try intermittently meeting resistance and torment

indicators.note: intermittently means taking every other letter of Meagre try, starting with the first

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A feeble rugby try met with opposition brings misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting' simply joins the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to make a sufferer of someone is to torment or persecute them.

clue.text: Elton with a piano cut short broadcast from somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread and rearranged
cut short says the word piano loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Elton John and his piano, briefly, on a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' trims PIANO to PIAN; ELTON + A + PIAN is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to Naples, a city in southern Italy.

clue.text: Ancient history that could be all spin

definitions.meaning: something that is ancient history is finished and done with
in cricket, a set of six deliveries from one bowler, which a spin bowler could deliver entirely as spin

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the six-ball unit bowled from one end is named by this word; a spinner bowls every ball of it with spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished events are ancient history; the cricket unit of six deliveries can consist entirely of spin bowling.

clue.text: Managed to get into terrible rage in class

indicators.note: to get into says one piece goes inside the other
terrible signals that the letters of rage are mangled into another order

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone managed to fly into a terrible temper during a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a schoolroom noun but is a verb meaning sort. 'Terrible' scrambles the rage letters to ARGE, and 'to get into' places the managed word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To class things is to sort or classify them, which is to put them in order.

clue.text: Performer after free ticket? This can be crushing

indicators.note: after says the performer comes second, following the ticket

parts.note: a comp is short for a complimentary, a free ticket
an actor is a stage or screen performer

explanation.surface: A performer turns up after getting a free ticket, and it proves crushing.
explanation.definitionFit: This machine squeezes rubbish or other material into a smaller mass, so its whole job is crushing.

clue.text: State colour required for layer

parts.note: Rhode Island is the smallest US state
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A colour is required for a layer of paint representing a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' suggests a coat of paint; it is a hen, something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known breed of domestic chicken kept for its egg production, so it is a laying hen.

clue.text: Cultivate pear hybrid to secure new funding

indicators.note: to secure means to hold something within, so one piece is placed inside
a hybrid is a cross-breed, signalling the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A grower breeds a new pear hybrid to attract investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hybrid' rearranges CULTIVATE PEAR, and N goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: This is money invested in a new or growing business, a form of funding for start-ups.

clue.text: Tastefully restrict endless urge to check former bald patch

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: to check means to hold back, here by sitting inside and stopping the other piece

parts.note: a pate is the crown of the head, often the bald patch

indicators.note: endless says the word urge loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An odd scene of someone restraining an urge to inspect an old bald spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of urge, leaving URG; 'to check' means holding it within the bald patch word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowdlerise a text is to remove offensive material from it, censoring it in the name of good taste.

clue.text: In retrospect Bob Marley by and large a hero on screen

indicators.note: In retrospect says the hidden letters are read backwards
by and large means mostly, so most of the words Bob Marley supply the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking back on Bob Marley, he was by and large a screen hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'by and large' in the definition; it is the hidden-word signal, as the blog says: most of BOB MAR(LEY) is used, then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: John Rambo is the action hero played by Sylvester Stallone in the First Blood films.

clue.text: What John Peel might have called house record previously

definitions.text: What John Peel might have called

indicators.note: previously says the record comes before the house

parts.note: a tally is a running record or count

explanation.surface: The DJ John Peel playing a house music record earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel suggests the BBC radio DJ, but the clue means the huntsman of the old song 'D'ye ken John Peel'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cry a fox hunter gives on sighting the quarry, so a huntsman like Peel would shout it.

clue.text: Insecure United fans agitated with point

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of fans are jumbled

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: United's supporters are anxious and agitated, with only a point to show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' rearranges FANS into NSAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is not safe, open to danger or collapse.

clue.text: Zero character shown in billet-doux

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring
a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A cipher symbol appears in a romantic note.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet-doux is French for a sweet note, a romantic message sent to a beloved.

clue.text: Remove prow from vessel to make another

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a boat, so the first letter of the vessel word is taken off

parts.note: a craft is a boat or vessel

explanation.surface: Taking the bow off one boat to build a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple floating platform is itself a kind of boat, so it is another vessel.

clue.text: Love line in continuous suite

indicators.note: in says the two letters go inside the other word

parts.note: flowing means continuous, without breaks
love is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A love song written as one line in a continuous musical suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suite' suggests music or rooms; here it is a retinue of attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite in its old sense is a body of attendants, a retinue or entourage of followers.

clue.text: Twirls rake, with mine about set to go west

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mine word wraps around the rake

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
a roue is a rake, a dissolute man

indicators.note: to go west in an across clue means reading right to left, so the word set runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rake and a mining set heading westward, oddly described as twirls.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'to go west' means right to left, giving TES; 'about' wraps the mine word round the rake.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet these are full spins on one foot, so they are twirls.

clue.text: Urbane sect I quit without a cent

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters a and cent are removed

parts.note: vacated means quit, as in left a building

explanation.surface: A member left a refined sect without a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' takes A and C out of VACATED, leaving VATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone urbane is polished and refined, which matches being well educated in manners and taste.

clue.text: Showing awareness

definitions.meaning: something showing is visible, within view (split as two words)
deep understanding or perception of a situation

explanation.walkthrough: Split two-five the answer means visible; as one word it means perception.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means visible; as one word it is penetrating understanding or perception.

clue.text: Sharapova's losing start causing strain

indicators.note: losing start says the first letter of her first name is dropped

parts.note: Maria Sharapova is the Russian tennis champion

explanation.surface: Sharapova losing her opening game puts her under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like tension; here it is a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music or tune, and this is a solo song in opera.

clue.text: Southern concern about cold is rare

indicators.note: about means around, so the concern word encloses the letter for cold

parts.note: care means concern or worry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Worry in the South about cold weather is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to find or in short supply is rare.

clue.text: Head of Penguin right to sack author

indicators.note: Head of means the first letter of Penguin

parts.note: to oust is to sack or remove from office

explanation.surface: The head of Penguin Books has the right to fire a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Penguin is a major publisher, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was the French writer of In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Got away with drugs wearing part of Superman costume

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so drugs in the plural are Es
Superman wears a cape, so someone wearing that part is caped

explanation.surface: Someone avoided arrest while carrying drugs and dressed in a Superman outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like a container signal; the whole phrase simply means CAPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fled or broken free from captivity is to have got away.

clue.text: Corrective pressure on the way up

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way or road

explanation.surface: Corrective pressure being applied that rises over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places P above the reversed LANE, as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to punishment of offenders, as in a punitive institution meant to correct behaviour.

clue.text: Roobarb originally a French character

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of Roobarb is used

parts.note: une is French for a

explanation.surface: Roobarb was originally a French cartoon character.
explanation.walkthrough: Roobarb is a British children's cartoon dog from the 1970s; 'character' looks like a cartoon figure but means a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet, so it is a written character.

clue.text: Quality cup of tea?

definitions.meaning: a quality is an attribute or feature of something
one's cup of tea is what one likes, one's personal preference

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup of tea' is British idiom for what someone likes: 'not my cup of tea'.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic is a thing about someone; and a favourite activity is your thing, your cup of tea.

clue.text: Express can unexpectedly echo opinion

parts.note: to utter is to express in words

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals that the letters of can come in a surprise order

parts.note: Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E

explanation.surface: An express train can unexpectedly echo a passenger's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges CAN into ANC.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken statement or expression of a view is a voiced opinion.

clue.text: Gently embracing Dicky her date in jest

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the gently word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: lightly means gently

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dicky gently hugs his date, just playfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but means unsound, rearranging HER DATE into HEARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in jest means doing it playfully, cheerfully and without seriousness.
